definition: In artificial intelligence and cognitive science, the structure mapping engine (SME) is an implementation in software of an algorithm for analogical matching based on the psychological theory of Dedre Gentner.
details: The basis of Gentner's structure-mapping idea is that an analogy is a mapping of knowledge from one domain (the base) into another (the target). The structure-mapping engine is a computer simulation of the analogy and similarity comparisons. The theory is useful because it ignores surface features and finds matches between potentially very different things if they have the same representational structure. For example, SME could determine that a pen is like a sponge because both are involved in dispensing liquid, even though they do this very differently.

explainer.lead: Software implementation of an algorithm for analogical matching based on Dedre Gentner's structure-mapping theory. It matters because it finds analogies between domains that look nothing alike, provided their relational structure matches.

tiers.eli5: It compares two things by how they are put together, not by what they are made of—so it can see a pen is to writing as a sponge is to soaking up, because both sit in the same kind of setup.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to retrieve and score analogies between structured representations; a common pitfall is expecting it to work on raw text, since it needs knowledge represented as relations and entities first.
tiers.paperLevel: An analogy is a mapping of knowledge from a base domain into a target domain; SME simulates analogy and similarity comparisons by aligning representational structure and preferring relational matches over surface features.

explainer.example: Given representations of a pen and a sponge, SME determines they are alike because both are involved in comparable relational roles rather than shared attributes.
